evals.prompt: Clients cannot connect with Kerberos to our SQL AG listener — they fall back to NTLM. I have setspn output and AD attributes for the service account. What is missing?
evals.expected_output: Flags the missing AG listener SPN as K12 (not K1/K3, which cover the instance hostname forms). Checks for duplicate SPN (K8), unconstrained delegation on the service account (K19), and delegation configuration (K21 KCD / K24 RBCD). Fix commands use setspn -S, never setspn -A, because -S validates that no duplicate exists first. States that the listener SPN is registered once against the replicas' shared service account, and that every instance in the WSFC cluster must run under that same account.

evals.prompt: We have unconstrained delegation on the SQL service account. Is this dangerous?
evals.expected_output: Flags K19 (unconstrained delegation) as Critical — not K20, which is the NTLM fallback signal. Explains the risk: the account can forward any user's credentials to any service, so a host compromise yields impersonation of any connecting user. Recommends migration to KCD (K21) or RBCD (K24) with PowerShell commands. Notes the two documented exceptions where unconstrained delegation is required rather than wrong: SSISDB catalog double-hop (K43), and linked servers below SQL 2017 CU17 (K42).

evals.prompt: Our linked server double-hop still lands as ANONYMOUS LOGON. We already set up resource-based constrained delegation on the target and the SPNs all check out. What now?
evals.expected_output: Identifies K41: linked servers do not support resource-based constrained delegation in any version. Directs to classic constrained delegation on the middle-tier account, gated at SQL Server 2017 CU17 or later (K42), or full delegation below that build. Does not recommend adding TrustedToAuthForDelegation to make RBCD work (K37) — the KDC always allows protocol transition under RBCD and the flag has no effect on that path.

evals.prompt: Windows Authentication broke for everyone this morning. Nothing changed on the SQL Server. The AD team says they disabled RC4 in the domain over the weekend.
evals.expected_output: Identifies K47: the service account resolves to RC4 only, either because msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes is 4 or because it is unset and DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes was hardened. Expects KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOTSUPP (0xE) in events 4768/4769 as confirming evidence. Fix is Set-ADUser -KerberosEncryptionType AES128,AES256, plus a password reset if the account predates AES support and therefore holds no AES keys. Does not report this as an SPN defect.
